qs.q: A cell biologist is studying metabolic organelles involved in cellular detoxification and lipid metabolism. Which biochemical feature distinguishes these specific organelles from lysosomes?
o: They primarily contain oxidative enzymes rather than hydrolases
They maintain an acidic internal environment via proton pumps
They utilize acid hydrolases for macromolecule breakdown
They are formed by budding from the trans-Golgi network
qs.e: Peroxisomes contain oxidases and catalases rather than the acidic hydrolases found in lysosomes. Lysosomes specialize in acid-dependent macromolecule degradation rather than oxidative metabolism.

qs.q: How does Growth Hormone affect lipid metabolism during periods of fasting?
o: It inhibits the breakdown of triglycerides to preserve fat stores
It promotes intense lipogenesis to store circulating fatty acids in adipose tissue
It stimulates lipolysis to provide fatty acids as an energy source
It converts excess fatty acids directly into hepatic glycogen stores
qs.e: GH stimulates lipolysis, the breakdown of fats, to provide fatty acids as an energy source during fasting. It does not promote lipogenesis or inhibit triglyceride breakdown.
qs.s: Receptors and Growth Hormone Signaling: MCQs

qs.q: A 54-year-old man undergoes biochemical evaluation of lipid metabolism and steroidogenesis. Which biochemical structural scaffold serves as the fundamental backbone for all classes of steroid hormones?
o: Terpenoid branched carbon skeleton
Isoprene subunit polymer chain
Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon core
Cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene ring
qs.e: All steroid hormones share a core cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene ring, commonly referred to as the steroid nucleus. Isoprene subunits serve as the foundational building blocks for terpenes rather than the core steroid skeleton.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the primary clinical use of lipid metabolism investigations such as HDL-C and LDL-C?
o: Evaluating acute fluid balance and acid-base status
Diagnosing acute hepatocellular injury and cholestasis
Assessing cardiovascular risk and treatment monitoring
Screening for and monitoring diabetes mellitus
qs.e: Lipid metabolism investigations including total cholesterol and LDL-C are used for cardiovascular risk assessment and treatment monitoring. They are distinct from liver biochemistry tests which assess hepatocellular injury.
qs.s: Clinical Biochemistry and Laboratory Testing: Foundations and Workflow: MCQs

qs.q: What percentage of sporadic colon cancers might be affected by lipid metabolism through APC gene mutations?
o: Approximately seventy percent.
Approximately fifty percent.
One hundred percent.
